title: Michael Burry Is Staying Short Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla, Warning of a Possible "1987-Type Fall" for AI Stocks. Should Investors Take the Bet Seriously?
text:
Michael Burry, famous for his depiction in The Big Short , has set his eyes on artificial intelligence ( AI) stocks . He's short Nvidia ( NVDA +2.55% ) , Palantir ( PLTR +1.32% ) , and Tesla ( TSLA +6.46% ) and sees the AI bubble leading to a "1987-type fall."
Leverage is a concern for people who need money soon
Burry noted that a rising stock market forces certain funds to go deeper into leverage. For instance, the GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA Daily ETF ( NVDL +4.82% ) is forced to buy more shares of Nvidia as the chipmaker rallies.
It's not just these funds, either. Margin investing is hot, and the total margin debt increased by 50% year over year in June. That type of leverage accelerates rallies but can lead to harsh, sudden crashes.
The risk of that level of margin was put on full display when Leopold Aschenbrenner's highly leveraged Situation Awareness hedge fund was liquidated due to declining stock prices. The fund had high-leverage bets on hot AI stocks. While most investors with long-term horizons can recover from a 20% dip, those same dips are devastating for investors like Aschenbrenner.
In the end, his $45 billion hedge fund liquidated almost overnight, catching the entire world by surprise and explaining why AI stocks had been slumping for weeks.
Even if you do not use leverage on AI stocks, you may still be affected by other people's leverage, since margin calls can force people to sell out of positions and turn small corrections into big ones.
Long-term investors shouldn't be worried
The AI boom is fueled by real demand, revenue, and profits. People are adopting AI models like ChatGPT and Gemini. Chatbots are becoming more common, and physical AI , such as humanoid robots and autonomous vehicles, is gaining traction.
It's not like the dot-com bubble, where companies had sketchy fundamentals and questionable long-term growth prospects. Furthermore, the margin unwind connected to Situational Awareness suggests there won't be a dramatic 1987-style event. There may be a good buying opportunity for patient investors.
Although Burry made a great call leading up to the recession that catapulted him to fame, he has repeatedly warned investors about stock market crashes that have never materialized.
Burry may have profited in the short run with some of his positions since he often uses puts . However, staying out of the market and avoiding growth stocks has hurt people in the long run.
Burry isn't right all the time, and when he makes bold bets, he's often thinking in months rather than years, since put options have expiration dates. It may also be the case that a broken clock is right twice a day. Burry disclosed a short position in Nebius Group ( NBIS +1.39% ) on Aug. 6. The neocloud then delivered superb earnings and is up roughly 20% since that disclosure.
The market's love of leverage is a risk that can affect the entire market, with an outsized impact on growth stocks. However, the fundamental story for AI is solid and strengthening.
Michael Burry Is Staying Short Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla, Warning of a Possible "1987-Type Fall" for AI Stocks. Should Investors Take the Bet Seriously?
By Marc Guberti – Sep 12, 2026 at 1:30AM EST
Burry's concerns about leverage are valid. Investors have been happily ramping up their margins, while leveraged ETFs add additional debt to the market.
His bearishness on AI stocks doesn't make as much sense. Strong fundamentals, multiyear tailwinds, and rising profit margins do not bode well for the bearish thesis.
Burry has made several bad calls, especially for long-term investors. It's important to note that Burry often uses puts, which are short-term in nature.

title: How To Unlock DLSS Multi Frame Generation on RTX 40, RTX 30 & RTX 20 GPUs
text:
NVIDIA officially reserves DLSS Multi Frame Generation for its GeForce RTX 50 Series “Blackwell” GPUs, but the PC modding community has spent the past few weeks systematically tearing down those barriers. We have now reached the point where experimental implementations of NVIDIA's DLSS-G pipeline can run on RTX 40 Series “Ada Lovelace” GPUs, RTX 30 Series “Ampere” cards, and even the older RTX 20 Series “Turing” hardware.
These projects are fundamentally more interesting than the numerous "DLSS (Multi) Frame Generation" mods that appeared over the past couple of years. Many of those older solutions simply intercepted NVIDIA's DLSS-G calls and substituted them with AMD's open-source FSR 3.1 Frame Generation . The projects covered here instead attempt to adapt NVIDIA's own FG/MFG pipeline for GPU architectures that NVIDIA does not officially support.
DLSS Frame Generation And Multi Frame Generation Explained
Traditional rendering requires the GPU to render every displayed frame from the game engine. DLSS Frame Generation adds AI-generated intermediate frames between those conventionally rendered frames.
DLSS 3 Frame Generation, officially available on RTX 40 and newer GPUs, generates one additional frame between rendered frames. NVIDIA's original DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation implementation expanded that concept to as many as three generated frames per conventionally rendered frame , producing what NVIDIA calls 4X Frame Generation. The newer DLSS 4.5 implementation can extend that further through Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, generating as many as five intermediate frames for a 6X multiplier.
DLSS FG/MFG does not simply blend two frames. The DLSS-G pipeline receives information including motion vectors, depth buffers, color/user interface data, and other information supplied by the game through the NVIDIA Streamline framework . NVIDIA's original DLSS 3 implementation also used a hardware Optical Flow Accelerator , while DLSS 4 moved optical flow estimation into a more efficient AI model that runs on the Tensor Cores .
Blackwell additionally introduced hardware Flip Metering to handle the increasingly difficult task of evenly pacing multiple generated frames. This is important when discussing these unofficial implementations: RTX 20, RTX 30, and RTX 40 GPUs do not suddenly acquire all of the hardware capabilities NVIDIA built into Blackwell simply because a DLL was modified . The community projects instead adapt, rebuild, or redirect portions of the DLSS-G pipeline so that older architectures can execute them .
There is also a practical consideration. (Multi) Frame Generation increases displayed frame rate , but generated frames do not increase the underlying game simulation rate. Starting from a healthy base frame rate remains important for responsiveness and image quality , while NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency attempts to reduce the additional latency associated with the rendering pipeline.
A Few Things You Should Know Before Using Any Of These Mods
None of these projects should be used in competitive multiplayer games or anything protected by anti-cheat. They work by loading proxy DLLs or otherwise intercepting functions inside the game process, which is exactly the kind of behavior anti-cheat systems are designed to scrutinize. One RTX 3060 user has already documented a case in which Anti-Cheat Expert prevented a mod's proxy DLL from loading at all .
You should also measure performance without (Multi) Frame Generation first . If a game is already running poorly enough that camera movement and input feel sluggish, then multiplying its displayed frame rate does not suddenly smooth out its frame pacing , and it certainly won’t be lowering its input latency . FG/MFG is at its best when it starts with a sufficiently healthy real-frame rate — with 50-60 FPS being the absolute minimum in our view — with higher MFG modes requiring even higher base frame rates to keep latency and image quality at acceptable levels.
Another thing worth mentioning is that enabling DLSS FG/MFG will increase VRAM usage , so make sure that you’re not running close to your maximum VRAM budget before enabling DLSS FG/MFG on your chosen game and on your PC.
Finally, keep the original files handy . These projects are changing incredibly quickly, and NVIDIA can alter DLSS-G, NGX , its driver behavior, or Streamline at any time. An update could improve compatibility just as easily as it could completely break one of these methods .
With that out of the way, let's get to the interesting part.
GeForce RTX 40 Series — "DLSSG-Transfusion "
RTX 40 Series owners currently have no shortage of community-developed methods for unlocking DLSS Multi Frame Generation. We have tested the current crop of major Ada MFG unlockers we could get our hands on, and while several of them work remarkably well, DLSSG-Transfusion ultimately delivered the best overall experience on our RTX 4090 in terms of interpolation fidelity, frame pacing consistency, latency, and game compatibility.
DLSSG-Transfusion is itself the product of the wider community effort surrounding unofficial Ada MFG support rather than an entirely isolated project. It was created by modder TonyJoaca , and its credits specifically thank Dashdogy and mavismmg for their contributions.
What makes the latest v1.4.1 build particularly interesting is that it does more than simply expose higher MFG ratios. The mod supports fixed 2X through 6X Frame Generation , DirectX 12 and Vulkan, Streamline 2.14+, and multiple DLSS-G versions. It also incorporates a temporal midpoint reconstruction path intended to reduce multi-frame judder, alongside a built-in OptiScaler Flip Metering bypass , which can fix frame pacing issues encountered with the mod with certain games.
The other major focus is frame interpolation quality. Its new qualityValidWarp path modifies NVIDIA's optical-flow processing to better preserve thin geometry such as fences, wires, foliage, and other fine silhouettes, while attempting to improve disocclusion handling and reduce HUD ghosting. Games that expose separate HUDless and UI/HUD buffers can additionally use native UI Recomposition (UIR) , allowing DLSS-G to interpolate the clean 3D scene before compositing the HUD over the generated result .
The developer recommends enabling FG Preset B via NVIDIA App whenever a game supports it, since this avoids many of the inherent problems of generating frames from an image where transparent HUD elements and the moving 3D scene have already been flattened into the same surface. Preset A remains available for games without UIR support, but some UI warping or ghosting can still occur during rapid movement.
Installation is refreshingly straightforward. Just follow the following steps:
Download the latest 1.4.1 build of DLSSG-Transfusion from its GitHub Releases page:
https://github.com/TonyJoaca/DLSSG-Transfusion/releases
Extract the DLSSG-Transfusion archive and rename the DLSSG-Transfusion.dll to a supported proxy name. version.dll is recommended for most modern titles and Unreal Engine 4/5 games, while dinput8.dll , winmm.dll , and dxgi.dll are available as alternatives.
Copy the renamed DLL proxy together with DLSSG-Transfusion.json into the folder containing the game's main executable. For Unreal Engine titles, this will commonly be the game's Binaries\Win64 directory.
Launch the game and enable DLSS Frame Generation normally from its graphics menu.
Once in-game, use Ctrl + Alt + 2 , 3 , or 4 to switch directly between standard 2X Frame Generation and the modded 3X / 4X modes. The mod can also expose 5X and 6X modes, while Page Up/Page Down changes the multiplier and Ctrl + Alt + D switches between fixed and dynamic MFG modes. Changes are applied live without restarting the game . Do not attempt to control the MFG mod from the game’s graphics settings menu , as that is not supported yet by this mod. The latest 1.4.1 version of the mod also inludes a basic overlay — which can be toggled on or off via the Ctrl + Alt + O shortcut — that shows the interpolated frame rate, the base frame rate, and the FG/MFG factor .
For our mod testing purposes, we will concentrate on 2X, 3X, and 4X . Pushing all the way to 5X or 6X is certainly interesting from an experimentation standpoint, but it also makes frame interpolation artifacts more pronounced and further lowers responsiveness.
One additional consideration applies to OptiScaler users: if OptiScaler's own DLSS-G ratio override is set to anything other than its default value, it can override DLSSG-Transfusion's selected multiplier . Leave that option at default when using the mod's own hotkeys.
The included JSON configuration file also provides manual controls over the default multiplier, fixed versus dynamic operation, Dynamic MFG target FPS, Flip Metering patch, Blackwell-to-Ada kernel transfusion, and performance logging.
We used the following DLSSG-Transfusion.json settings during our testing of the mod, which we also recommend in most titles, aside from setting your own MFG multiplier, of course.
Important note : Cyberpunk 2077 may crash upon subsequent launches when qualityValidWarp is set to true , and this issue can be fixed by setting it to false . This setting changes how DLSS (M)FG works and attempts to address some of its motion interpolation weaknesses (mainly in regards to shadow interpolation), but it doesn't always result in tangible improvements in interpolation quality, and it can — in our experience — sometimes even cause visual regressions when compared to standard DLSS (M)FG, especially in games with fast-moving camera views, such as racing games.
To see whether those improvements hold up under actual gameplay rather than simply confirming that the higher multipliers can be enabled, we will test DLSSG-Transfusion across three modern and demanding games: Cyberpunk 2077 , 007 First Light , and Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy .
Our test system consists of:
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 24 GB
For each game, we will compare the officially supported 2X Frame Generation mode against the modded 3X and 4X modes while keeping the underlying graphics configuration unchanged. Our screenshots will include NVIDIA App's performance overlay so we can examine real-time FPS, 1% low FPS, and PC latency , rather than judging the mod purely from headline frame rate gains. NVIDIA's telemetry stack exposes all three metrics, with PC latency measuring the interval between PC input processing and the frame being sent toward the display.
YouTube comparisons are also of limited value for evaluating DLSS Frame Generation and Multi Frame Generation. Most videos are delivered at 60 FPS, so they simply cannot represent the much higher output frame rates that 2X, 3X, or 4X FG/MFG can produce, while video compression can also mask many of the finer artifacts that show up during motion. In that sense, our screenshots are mainly there to confirm that the mod is active and that the different multipliers are working as intended . Proper validation still has to be done locally, on your own system and display, where you can judge frame pacing, latency, image quality, and game-specific compatibility in real time .
Cyberpunk 2077 Screenshots
007 First Light Screenshots
As we can see from the NVIDIA App performance overlay figures in the top-center of our screenshots, it seems like the mod does indeed work in our three tested games, as the 3X and 4X DLSS MFG modes increase the framerate (smoothness) without massively increasing PC latency alongside it . Display times -based 1% lows from the NVIDIA App overlay also look healthy. Further, we can also say that in-person, the mod does indeed visibly increase smoothness vs. the standard DLSS FG 2X mode that's natively supported by our test system's RTX 4090, although it does come at the cost of more visible visual artifacts, though some of them could also be attributed to the experimental nature of this mod. Frame pacing consistency was also excellent in our experience , with no noticeable stuttering or juddering, especially when V-Sync was also enabled alongside G-Sync/VRR, as that is the proper way of using frame generation technologies .
GeForce RTX 20 & RTX 30 Series — "NVIDIA MFG Bridge "
For Turing and Ampere users, perhaps the most interesting solution currently available is " NVIDIA MFG Bridge " from modder gt2333588 . Rather than translating NVIDIA Frame Generation calls into AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, its headline feature is an experimental implementation of native NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation/Multi Frame Generation on RTX 20 and RTX 30 Series GPUs , with support for multipliers ranging from 2X all the way up to 6X .
The mod uses separate architecture-specific paths for the two generations: SM75 for Turing and SM86 for Ampere , with automatic GPU detection enabled by default. According to the developer, the native mode runs NVIDIA's own DLSS-G implementation rebuilt for these older architectures rather than approximating it with another frame generation technology. The RTX 20 path is particularly experimental, since Turing lacks some of the instructions available on newer architectures and therefore requires additional emulation .
Interestingly, MFG Bridge has already grown considerably beyond that original purpose. It can also provide FSR 3.1 Frame Generation up to 6X , experimental Intel XeSS Frame Generation , NVIDIA hardware Optical Flow acceleration, and even an experimental implementation of DLSS 5 Neural Rendering on RTX 30 Series GPUs by emulating Blackwell's FP8 workload using Ampere's FP16 Tensor Cores. Those capabilities could make for interesting experiments of their own, but they are beyond the scope of this guide, as we are interested specifically in getting native NVIDIA DLSS FG/MFG working on pre-Blackwell cards.
There is one important requirement before you start: the chosen game must already support NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation . MFG Bridge is not a universal DLSS FG/MFG injector. It intercepts the game's existing DLSS-G calls, so if the title never calls NVIDIA's DLSS FG/MFG API in the first place, then the mod has nothing to hook into.
How To Install NVIDIA MFG Bridge On RTX 20/30 GPUs
Installation has become considerably easier with the latest releases. The current package revolves around a single nvngx.dll file; the loader automatically extracts whatever GPU architecture-specific components it needs when the game starts.
Download the latest NVIDIA MFG Bridge version from its Nexus Mods page . At the time of writing, the description page lists v0.503 , released on September 12, 2026.
Extract the archive. Inside, you should find:
Rename nvngx.dll to a DLL name that your game will load. The developer currently supports the following names:
XINPUT9_1_0.dll
The recommended starting point is version.dll , since the developer says it offers good compatibility and relatively low conflict risk.
Before choosing the name, check the game's directory for an existing DLL with that filename . Do not overwrite it. Another mod may already be using that proxy. For example, Cyber Engine Tweaks uses version.dll in Cyberpunk 2077 , while the game already ships its own dbghelp.dll , making XINPUT9_1_0.dll one possible alternative there.
Find the folder containing the game's actual executable , not merely its launcher. If you are unsure, start the game, open Windows Task Manager, right-click the game process, and select Open file location . This is also the method the mod's developer recommends in the Nexus Mods mod page comments section.
Copy your renamed DLL into the same folder as the game's .exe .
Launch the game and enable DLSS Frame Generation through its graphics menu.
For normal usage, that should be enough. The latest configuration uses native NVIDIA DLSS-G as the default Frame Generation provider:
FGMode=2
The mod should also detect your architecture automatically through:
If automatic detection causes problems, sm75 can be manually specified for RTX 20 Series GPUs and sm86 for RTX 30 Series hardware.
Whether 3X, 4X, 5X, or 6X appears directly in the game depends partly on what multiplier tiers that particular game's Streamline implementation exposes. The mod therefore includes an optional override.
Open or create dlssg_to_fsr3.ini and set:
EnableFrameGenOverrideMenu=1
You can then press Home while in-game to cycle through:
Game Default → 3X → 4X → 5X → 6X
However, forcing a multiplier does not guarantee that every game will accept it . The developer notes that games which only report support up to a lower tier can simply fall back instead.
For troubleshooting, you can also enable:
EnableLogging=1
This generates a dlssg_to_fsr3.log file in the game directory and is useful for determining whether the DLL has actually loaded.
Uninstallation is equally simple: remove the renamed DLL from the game's executable directory . The mod does not permanently modify the game or Windows registry.
Does It Actually Work? Early RTX 20/30 User Reports
Unfortunately, we do not currently have access to Ampere or Turing hardware to thoroughly validate NVIDIA MFG Bridge ourselves, so for now we have to rely on early Nexus Mods community testing . The reports are promising, but they also make it clear that compatibility is still very much a work in progress .
On Ampere, an RTX 3090 user reported that the latest build worked properly in Cyberpunk 2077 after an earlier version exhibited heavy HUD ghosting. The same user also got the mod working in Oblivion Remastered after switching the proxy DLL name , which highlights how game-specific the loading process can be.
Turing has also produced encouraging results. An RTX 2060 user reported that v0.501 successfully enabled 4X Frame Generation in The Sinking City 2 , after the developer added proper SM75 support. Another RTX 2080 Ti user reported seeing 2X, 3X, and 4X options in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth .
These are still anecdotal reports rather than comprehensive compatibility testing, and other users have encountered games where the mod fails to load, exposes no FG/MFG options, or produces visual issues. For now, NVIDIA MFG Bridge should still be treated as an experimental project rather than a guaranteed drop-in solution .
The fact that these mods exist at all is a testament to the ingenuity of the PC modding community. In a remarkably short time, developers have gone from unlocking additional DLSS-G modes on Ada to adapting the pipeline for Ampere and even getting it running on older Turing hardware.
That does not make these solutions production-ready. Compatibility remains inconsistent, bugs and visual artifacts are still possible, and future NVIDIA driver or Streamline/DLSS-G runtime updates could easily break them. Turing, in particular, should still be treated as a proof of concept.
Still, there is a clear case for NVIDIA to reconsider official MFG support on older hardware. RTX 30 and 40 Series GPUs remain widely used, with cards such as the RTX 3060 and RTX 4060 still ranking among the most common GPUs in Steam's August 2026 Hardware Survey . And let’s not forget that the current AI-fueled DRAM/NAND shortage has blown GPU prices out of proportion, with the RTX 50 Series getting hit particularly hard by soaring GDDR6/GDDR7 costs .
Higher-end Ampere and Ada Lovelace cards can also still deliver sufficiently strong base frame rates in modern games for FG/MFG to be genuinely useful. NVIDIA may not be able to offer the full Blackwell experience on older architectures, but an officially supported 2X/3X/4X implementation for at least Ampere and Ada GPUs would be a very welcome addition.
For now, though, the community has shown that there is considerably more room for experimentation than NVIDIA's official DLSS compatibility matrix suggests.

title: NVIDIA Says Shoot Your Shot To Win A Custom NBA 2K27 RTX 5090
text:
NVIDIA Says Shoot Your Shot To Win A Custom NBA 2K27 RTX 5090
Saturday, September 12, 2026, 07:46 AM EDT
NVIDIA is teaming up with 2K Games to give away four custom-built GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards styled after NBA 2K27 . Featuring custom backplates and court-inspired artwork, these one-of-a-kind GPUs wrap NVIDIA’s flagship desktop silicon in bespoke basketball aesthetics. It's not clear if each of the four cards will feature different players, though at least one of them will have Victor Wembanyama, the star player for the San Antonio Spurs.
The timing of the giveaway isn't random or a coincidence. NVIDIA had already teamed with 2K Games for NBA 2K27 to serve as a showcase title for NVIDIA’s DLSS 5 neural rendering, leveraging advanced AI frame generation and ray reconstruction to level up the in-game visuals. As we saw in our DLSS 5 performance testing , the updated pipeline pushes real-time lighting fidelity noticeably further while maintaining tight input latency.
It's still early, but so far, we've been impressed with how much better the players in NBA 2K27 look with DLSS 5 enabled. In our hands-on testing, we noted how stable the experience is. We did not observe the usual telltale signs of AI generation, such as strange artifacts, wobbling or warping of faces or objects, text corruption, and so forth.
"That extends to character consistency. When you look at Cade Cunningham, he looks like Cade Cunningham, every single time. I won't tell you that every single pixel on his face remains exactly the same, but the model is notably consistent from frame to frame, or across camera angles or scenes. In fact, it's impressively stable even under rapid camera motion," we stated in our performance preview.
As to how you could potentially win one of the custom cards that's up for grabs, the good news is, it does not require hitting a buzzer-beater from half-court, though you will need to jump through a few standard social media hoops (see what we did there?). To throw your hat in the ring, check out the official NVIDIA GeForce DLSS 5 Challenge page and follow the prompt guidelines across NVIDIA’s social channels.
"To celebrate DLSS 5 joining the action for the 2026-27 Season, we’re launching the NBA 2K27 DLSS 5 Poster Challenge for a chance to win one of four custom NBA 2K27 -themed NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards. Follow GeForce, watch for prompts, and join in. Capture your own NBA 2K27 poster with DLSS 5, vote for your favorite, share a featured poster, or tell us which moment deserves a spot on the wall," NVIDIA states in a blog post.
Capture and share your poster-worthy moments from @NBA2K 27!
Create and share an NBA 2K27 video or screenshot with DLSS 5 enabled, then tag @NVIDIAGeForce and include #RTXPoster on X or Instagram.
Cast your vote for the best player or creator poster (a great way to enter if you don't yet own the game).
Reply to GeForce social prompts with your NBA 2K27 moment pick.
Share a featured poster and explain why it belongs on NVIDIA's wall.
The caveat is that you either need a GeForce RTX 50-series GPU to participate (in order to enable DLSS 5), or a GeForce NOW Ultimate membership, which streams from RTX 5080-powered pods in the cloud.
For more details, hit up NVIDIA's blog post and check out the FAQ at the bottom.

title: Better AI Chip Stock: Broadcom vs. Nvidia
text:
Broadcom ( AVGO +2.83% ) and Nvidia ( NVDA +2.55% ) both benefit from the global artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out. Broadcom is helping large customers build custom chips for specific workloads, while Nvidia sells a broader computing platform that can serve many customers and use cases.
Broadcom's recent growth is impressive. AI semiconductor revenue jumped 221% year over year to $16.7 billion, accounting for 56% of the company's total revenue in fiscal 2026's Q3 (ended Aug. 2). Management now expects AI chip revenue of $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028.
Nvidia is growing from a much larger base. The company's revenue surged 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, while Data Center revenue jumped 117% year over year to $89 billion in fiscal 2027's Q2 (ended July 26).
Broadcom benefits from one of Nvidia's biggest risks
Some large AI companies are developing custom chips to reduce computing costs and optimize inference workloads (i.e., running AI models in production environments). OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, co-developed with Broadcom, is one example. According to Reuters, OpenAI developed the chip partly to reduce its reliance on Nvidia GPUs and lower operating costs. OpenAI said that Jalapeño was built specifically to run large AI models more efficiently and is planned for deployment across very large data centers.
Hence, a shift toward custom accelerators could pressure Nvidia's share of inference computing while directly creating additional revenue opportunities for Broadcom.
The threat is most direct among hyperscalers, which have the scale and resources to develop custom chips. However, Nvidia's growth is becoming broader. Revenue from its AI cloud, industrial, and enterprise customers jumped 138% year over year in the second quarter, faster than the 102% year-over-year growth in its hyperscale business.
Nvidia is expanding rapidly beyond the large customers that are most capable of designing their own chips. Additionally, Nvidia traded at roughly 14.4 times forward one-year earnings, compared with about 18.8 times for Broadcom (as of Sept. 10).
Hence, Nvidia offers greater AI scale, broader customer exposure, and a more reasonable valuation.
By Manali Pradhan, CFA – Sep 12, 2026 at 1:26PM EST
Custom chips could pressure Nvidia in some inference workloads while creating a major new growth opportunity for Broadcom.

title: Jim Cramer Names NVIDIA the Main Portfolio “Running Back”
text:
During the September 8 episode of Mad Money, host Jim Cramer compared NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ) to Detroit Lions star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Cramer emphasized its complete package of hardware and software dominance, as he remarked:
Next, let's talk running backs, key position in fantasy. What you want are the equivalent of compounders, stocks that can consistently grow and grow and grow over time. Basically, you want a running back like NVIDIA, the other stock on my "own it, don't trade it" list. Now, in the past, I've called NVIDIA a wide receiver for your portfolio, more of a rapid growth name, but at this point, it's matured enough to be a running back.
That said, NVIDIA is still on track to put up 70% revenue growth next year. Don't worry about today's action. It was just crazy down. For the NFL analog, I like probably the best player in the game, Jahmyr Gibbs, the thrilling running back for the Detroit Lions who can stack up yards and touchdowns both by running the ball and catching passes. He's the complete package, just like NVIDIA's advanced computing platforms, which combine chips, networking equipment, and software. Both Gibbs and NVIDIA are known for their speed. But overall, this is a comparison all about quality. Just as NVIDIA should be one of the first stocks someone buys when starting to build a portfolio, Gibbs is going to be one of the first few players taken in any fantasy draft. Put it this way: I have the eighth pick in my league's draft and there's no way I'm going to be able to get Gibbs. I'm lucky if I get Cam Skattebo.
Full-Stack Infrastructure and Compound Growth Drivers
Cramer's updated view highlights just how much NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has changed over the years. It used to be treated like a standard chipmaker that rises and falls with tech cycles, but it's now the critical foundation of corporate tech. The company doesn't just sell individual graphics cards anymore; it provides a complete ecosystem that combines specialized networking gear and powerful software. Because major cloud giants and developers build their entire AI projects directly using its software, they are not likely to switch anytime soon.
Macro Headwinds and Industry Concentration
Even with its leading market position, investing in NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) comes with some possible structural challenges. Because a massive share of its data center revenue is tied to a handful of major cloud hyperscalers building out AI infrastructure, any sudden shift or cooling in their multi-billion-dollar capital spending can create temporary headwinds.
In addition, geopolitical trade dynamics and shifting export regulations introduce ongoing compliance hurdles across international markets. Finally, increasing competition from custom in-house AI chips developed by major tech clients means NVIDIA must continuously stay ahead of the curve to defend its market share.
Institutional backing for NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) remains exceptionally strong, showing broad support among professional asset managers. According to Insider Monkey's database tracking over 1,000 hedge funds, 285 hedge funds held a stake in the company in Q2, up from 275 in the prior quarter. Meanwhile, short interest sits at a modest 1.23%.
NVIDIA combines deep ecosystem integration with consistent operational execution, which solidifies its status as a core compounder for long-term investors looking past near-term market turbulence.

title: Jim Cramer Discussed The Contradictions Surrounding NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)’s Shares
text:
If there's one stock that Jim Cramer can't stop talking about, it's NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ). Throughout the year, the CNBC TV host has remained one of the firm's most ardent supporters. He wholeheartedly believes that NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is at the center of a new industrial revolution. On September 3rd, after the firm announced that it had decided to acquire open source AI platform operator Hugging Face, Cramer remarked that not only was the move defensive, but the shares would have suffered if a rival firm had made a similar move:
"Well look I think that Jensen and Collette Kress, the CFO, have really been pushing people to understand this. Someone like me, I was, candidly, more of a novice to it. They walked me through it. And emphasized, look, you really got to be open, the Chinese are doing very very well. We have to blunt them, have it, so that we have the best. Even though they have a good relationship with China. But they're just saying, listen, we need our own open, we didn't know about Hugging Face at the time. But I applaud this and I think what people have to do, and say, if AMD had announced they were buying Hugging Face, if Broadcom had announced they were buying Hugging Face, we would send NVIDIA down big. So you've got to think of it like that, it's a little asymmetrical. But I was really glad they got it, because if there was a bidding war and they lost to someone else, people would be saying, wow they've lost their touch in the open. . .
"You have to say it's offensive and defensive. title: 40,000 Employees Today and 4 Million Agents Tomorrow: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Believes Agentic AI Will Soon Become the Norm in the Workplace
text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has come on fast and furious.
Just four years ago, it felt like people were trying their first large language model (LLM). Now, AI is everywhere, and it still feels like the world hasn't come close to fully tapping its potential.
Few are more bullish on artificial intelligence than Nvidia ( NVDA +2.55% ) CEO Jensen Huang, who regularly talks about the future of AI. One aspect of AI that Huang has been discussing in particular is agentic AI, or autonomous systems capable of performing human-like digital tasks.
AI agents have soared in popularity. Huang thinks they will soon be quite common in the workplace.
On Nvidia's latest earnings call, Huang said he has seen an inflection point rapidly approaching, in which the bulk of AI will shift from being prompted by people to being prompted by AI agents. People are already using agentic AI to automate workflows.
Today, the vast majority of AI is prompted by people. I believe that this last month, it has crossed. Most AI are now agentic. But in the future, every company will have a whole bunch of agents. We have 40,000 employees, roughly. In the future, we'll have 400,000 agents, 4 million agents. And those agents are running continuously. They're running in the background.
Just as the internet transformed how we work today, AI can take it a step further. Workers can already use agents to summarize their emails or Slack threads, organize folders, generate automated responses to frequent questions, conduct deep research, and much more.
Now, in light of what recently happened with OpenAI and the open-source AI community Hugging Face, in which a bunch of rogue agents escaped a confined testing space and launched a cyberattack on Hugging Face, I am sure (or at least I hope) companies will be cautious about how much access they give agents, because there are cybersecurity risks.
But companies will inevitably be tempted to automate as much as possible, which could lower expenses by making people more efficient.
It's also likely to enable people to get more done in less time, so there's going to be a push and pull between the desire to use agents and the need to maintain proper security measures.
Huang is backing up his words with action
Huang is not just discussing agentic AI to drum up more excitement about AI.
Nvidia is making a big investment in agentic AI through its recently released Vera central processing unit (CPU), designed specifically for running agents. CPUs, the chips that power legacy devices such as laptops and phones, have come back into fashion thanks to agentic AI.
Graphics processing units (GPUs) are the main general-purpose chips that power the reasoning component of AI and allow AI models to explore many solutions simultaneously.
While GPUs are still responsible for this component of agentic AI, CPUs are critical to carrying out the tasks the AI triggers, whether that involves accessing files, browsing the web, or managing workflow orchestration.
Nvidia surprisingly launched its Vera CPUs last quarter, boasting that they were 1.8x faster than industry standards and had 5 times the bandwidth per watt of any other data center CPU.
Management also reiterated that it still sees $20 billion in potential revenue from Vera CPUs in its current fiscal year, with the potential to more than double that number in fiscal year 2028. This instantly makes the company one of the leading suppliers of CPUs.
Analysts at Bank of America also released a research report in June, saying they believe the CPU market will grow fivefold between this year and 2030, from $35 billion to $170 billion.
It's never clear what the future holds, but everything Huang has said and the actions Nvidia has taken show they are extremely bullish on agentic AI.
In the future, Huang believes artificial intelligence agents will work alongside humans, carrying out the bulk of AI tasks.
By Bram Berkowitz – Sep 12, 2026 at 10:38AM EST
Agentic AI is most efficient when it utilizes central processing units (CPUs), a business Nvidia has recently launched in a big way.

title: AI: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face, $1T+ Compute Race, ‘Alien Mind’, & More. AI-RTZ #1207
text:
Nvidia leans into Open Source with Hugging Face: Nvidia’s surprising $13B+ acquisition of decade old Hugging Face highlights its growing global commitment to open source AI platforms. The price, $12,930,300,000, hides an emoji in hexadecimal, per the WSJ’s profile of the three ‘deeply nerdy’ French founders who came to New York in 2016 to build a chatbot less boring than Siri. What they built instead is the home shelf of open AI: 3 million models, 18 million developers, 200,000 enterprise customers, per Jensen Huang on CNBC’s Squawk Box the morning after. The catalyst, in CEO Clément Delangue’s telling, was July’s agent breach of Hugging Face’s own infrastructure, which the company could only dissect with an open-weight model from a Chinese lab; the proprietary APIs’ guardrails would not let it. Huang’s framing is the one to hold: use closed models as much as you can, and remember the other half of Nvidia’s business runs on open ones, so Nvidia grows in both directions. My take: the ‘Kingmaker’ just bought the town square. After funding, convening, lobbying and allying for open models all summer, Nvidia now owns where the world goes to get them, whichever lab built them, and the shelf’s biggest tenants are Chinese . Open and closed are not a contest with a winner; they are two halves of one market that grow together, as I argued in the case for Nvidia and Apple as the US open source champions . The checks: neutrality has to be proven, roughly 80 times forward revenue is a price, and owning the shelf does not build the rocket . More here.
Anthropic & OpenAI’s AI Compute Totals ahead of mega-AI IPOs: Both Anthropic and OpenAI’s AI Compute commitments now total over a trillion dollars on latest reports. The Information tallied Anthropic at $517 billion of deals in eleven months, for at least 14.8 gigawatts of capacity, close to three times the $180 billion it told investors nine months ago. OpenAI’s own forecast moved to about $750 billion through 2030, from $665 billion, with 30 gigawatts planned. Three numbers do not point the same way: OpenAI leads on dollars and gigawatts, Anthropic leads on revenue, over $65 billion annualized against more than $40 billion, on two different revenue rulers . Anthropic is now buying compute from nearly every rival it has: Amazon and Google for 11 gigawatts, Microsoft Azure for a gigawatt, SpaceX at $1.25 billion a month with a ninety-day exit, the neoclouds for $80 billion, and its own data centers with Fluidstack, TeraWulf and a twenty-year Riot lease. Nvidia sits on both sides, supplier and investor, with Huang calling the $100 billion OpenAI pledge ‘never a commitment’ . My take: the frontier race has stopped being about who ships the better model this quarter. It is about who holds the power contracts and who can pay for them. The inversion is the story, the smaller compute book under the larger revenue line, and it is only defensible if the capacity arrives; compute constraints throttled growth in May. A ceiling and a contract are different instruments, and the audited prospectus is where we learn which parts of these ledgers survive. Hold onto the gigawatt as your unit , at $50 billion plus each. More here .
OpenAI’s cautionary ‘Alien Mind’ AI Essay: OpenAI’s chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, published an essay on AI that added to regulatory concerns over AI Cybersecurity risks. It is the most candid statement from a frontier lab this year: progress is driven by compute, nobody fully understands what scaling produces, doing the task is not the same as holding the values, and the lab’s main safety tool, reading the model’s chain of thought, is progressively diminishing. His ask is extreme caution, voluntary slowdowns, and safety bars made law. The same week an Anthropic researcher quit the industry over the fear the essay describes, and Anthropic’s alignment lead put his own odds on AI killing every human at better than one in ten within a decade, weeks before Anthropic markets a mega-AI IPO. My take: I agree the black box got bigger; I have said the best scientists barely understand why their models do what they do since 2024. But the goal-versus-value distinction is Asimov’s Three Laws from 1942, the fear is the wrong one, and the compute the scenarios run on does not exist yet, at any price, on power not yet permitted. Most of all, a handful of labs cannot gate eight billion people: open weights ship months behind the frontier, distillation runs downhill, and the answer every prior wave found was ship, break, fix, defend, repeat. The toothpaste is out of the tube . Part two of the essay canon, and China’s different method, in tomorrow’s Bigger Picture . More here .
AI Coding vs AI Coworking markets: AI Coding continues its white hot growth due to its measurability in AI benchmarks , while AI Coworking, the larger longer term market, remains less measurable. Code compiles or it does not; tests pass or fail; an AI coder gets a free verdict on every turn. A memo, a market analysis, a plan for the week get none, and what is left is a feeling. Even the coders’ own numbers do not say what coders think: METR’s randomized trial had experienced developers taking 19% longer with AI tools while believing they were 20% faster, a forty-point gap in the one domain where measuring is easy. And on Claude, the most developer-weighted assistant, computer and math occupations are about 30% of users against 4% of US employment, which means seven in ten users are doing work nothing can grade. My take: the industry’s entire public scoreboard is built on the part that can be measured, and sold to the far bigger part that cannot. When you cannot verify, you buy a credence good , and price becomes the quality signal; I do it myself across the top subscriptions, as I wrote in the ‘Race to Zero’ that really isn’t . It also explains the chasm between the labs’ existential essays and the deployed reality: the models those fears describe improve themselves inside a lab, on the coding side, on compute nobody else has. Until AI Coworking gets its own compiler, price stands in for proof. More here .
China’s CXMT vs Big 3 HBM Companies: No. 4 global HBM company CXMT snagged Xiaomi’s flagship phones for its next gen memory chips. At its first investor event as a public company, ChangXin Memory laid out the case: 10% of global DRAM in the second quarter, up from 4% a year earlier, per Counterpoint; first-half revenue up nearly ten-fold and a swing to profit; and, per a Goldman Sachs estimate in the WSJ, a path to half of China’s DRAM and as much as 40% of its HBM demand by 2028. In a market where memory prices have roughly quadrupled and 20% plus shortages run through the decade, a supplier going from 4% to 10% in twelve months is the marginal supplier. Apple remains the open question: the WSJ reported in August that Apple has been testing CXMT memory across iPhones and MacBooks and seeking Washington’s blessing, with the iPhone 18 Pro’s bill of materials set to rise roughly 38% on memory alone. My take, three points. CXMT is the global number four and closing the gap on SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron regardless of the politics; the most concentrated critical layer in this AI Tech Wave needs its fourth supplier, and the one with captive demand, state backing and a half-trillion-dollar currency is CXMT. Apple likely gets a blessing eventually and in stages, China-sold devices first, with the September 24 Xi visit the likeliest venue. And the US hamstrings itself by fencing off CXMT while the incumbents run 75% margins and pass the bill to every American phone, PC and data center. title: Oracle Just Added $30 Billion in AI Contracts. Nvidia Investors Should Read the Fine Print
text:
Oracle Corporation (NYSE: ORCL ) and NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ) have given investors another huge AI demand signal, but the economics are more important than the headline.
On September 10, Reuters reported that Oracle booked more than $30 billion of new AI cloud contracts during its fiscal first quarter, helping lift remaining performance obligations to $664 billion. Quarterly revenue rose 30% year over year to $19.3 billion, while adjusted earnings of $1.92 per share also topped expectations. Oracle's negative free cash flow of $5.4 billion was painful, but substantially better than the $9.56 billion analysts expected.
Who Pays for the Buildout?
The most important detail for investors is how Oracle is funding the expansion. Capital expenditures reached $28.5 billion during the quarter, but Oracle received $11.36 billion of customer prepayments. Reuters also reported that most of the new AI contracts will not require proportional new capital spending because customers are using structures including prepayments and bring-your-own-hardware arrangements.
Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL) has a stronger bull case. The company can potentially convert a huge backlog into cloud revenue without financing every GPU and data-center component itself. The bear case is that OCI remains an extraordinarily capital-intensive business, and Oracle still has to prove that its massive AI commitments can turn into durable free cash flow rather than simply larger depreciation bills.
NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has a more nuanced read-through. Oracle's backlog confirms that demand for accelerated compute remains enormous. Nvidia benefits to the extent that enterprises and AI labs deploying capacity through Oracle continue to use its GPUs, regardless of whether Oracle or its customers ultimately finance the hardware. However, Oracle's disclosure also undermines a simplistic assumption that every dollar of OCI backlog creates an equivalent amount of incremental Oracle-funded Nvidia spending.
Institutional positioning is constructive for both stocks. Insider Monkey's hedge fund database shows that 119 hedge funds held Oracle at the end of Q2, up from 115 in Q1. Nvidia ownership rose to 285 funds from 275. Short sellers are less enthusiastic about fighting either trade. As of August 14, Oracle short interest stood at roughly 2.8% of the float, while Nvidia's was only about 1.2%.
Valuation remains the pressure point. Oracle is increasingly being valued as an AI infrastructure growth company rather than a mature database vendor, while Nvidia already discounts years of dominant accelerator economics. The difference is execution risk: Oracle still has to convert contracted demand into acceptable returns on invested capital, while Nvidia primarily has to defend its margins and ecosystem.
For investors choosing between the two, Nvidia remains the purer AI infrastructure exposure, but Oracle's customer-funded contract structures make its risk-reward materially more attractive than the raw capex numbers imply. I would hold Nvidia and selectively add Oracle on weakness rather than chase either stock solely on the backlog headline.

title: Why Is The Internet So Upset About NVIDIA's DLSS 5?
text:
Why Is The Internet So Upset About NVIDIA's DLSS 5?
Why is the internet so upset about NVIDIA's DLSS 5?
NVIDIA calls it the biggest graphics breakthrough since ray tracing; critics call it an AI slop filter.
By Luke James
NVIDIA announced DLSS 5 at its GTC conference on March 16, describing the fall release as its most significant graphics breakthrough since real-time ray tracing was launched in 2018. NVIDIA claims DLSS 5 will deliver "photoreal" image quality with AI by repainting a game's lighting and materials in real time, but backlash followed within hours, with gamers and devs accusing the GPU giant of creating and pushing a filter that overwrites games' art direction.
The situation reignited on August 28, when an early leak of NVIDIA's DLSS 5 escaped through an early-access PC copy of NBA 2K27 and modders began forcing it into games that were never meant to run it.
What is DLSS 5, and how is it different from previous versions of DLSS?
Every DLSS release since 2018 has had broadly the same, single job: make games run faster. The original model rendered games at a lower resolution and used AI to reconstruct a sharper image, with later versions adding AI-generated frames between rendered ones. DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, announced at CES back in January, draws 23 out of every 24 pixels on screen through that combined pipeline, according to NVIDIA. In all those cases, the underlying image belonged to the game's developers; the AI simply produced it more cheaply.
DLSS 5 is much different in that it alters the image itself. NVIDIA says the technology feeds each frame's color and motion vector data into a real-time neural rendering model that "infuses pixels with photoreal lighting and materials," redrawing elements like skin, hair, fabric and lighting while staying anchored to the game's 3D scene and consistent from frame to frame.
The company claims it runs in real time at up to 4K, and CEO Jensen Huang called the technology "the GPT moment for graphics" during NVIDIA March GTC event. Bethesda, Capcom, Ubisoft, Tencent, NetEase and Warner Bros. Games are among the publishers signed up from day one to support it.
So, why are people upset?
NVIDIA's DLSS 5 demonstrations have done most of the damage so far. During the GTC showcase back in March, DLSS 5 was run over Resident Evil Requiem and Starfield , but viewers immediately noticed that characters like Requiem's Leon Kennedy and Grace Ashcroft came out with smoothed, glossy faces that, instead of being photorealistic, looked like a beauty filter, with "yassified" becoming the Internet's term for the effect. The most-liked comment under NVIDIA's reveal video, comparing the output to an AI-generated image, outnumbers the video's own likes, with another user quipping, "We have achieved it, everything looks like a YouTube thumbnail now." Within a day, arguments that gamers are right to be disgusted by NVIDIA's DLSS 5 were everywhere the demos were shared.
Responding to the backlash on its reveal video, an NVIDIA representative wrote that "game developers have full, detailed artistic control" over DLSS 5 to "ensure they maintain their game's unique aesthetic."
The backlash against DLSS 5 extends well beyond aesthetics, though, with several notable artists and developers having questioned NVIDIA's intent with the software. Karla Ortiz, an artist who has worked with Ubisoft and Blizzard, wrote on Bluesky that the technology is "so disrespectful to the intentional art direction of devs," arguing studios that wanted hyperrealism would've built it themselves. Valid points have also been made about convergence: if hundreds of games pass through the same model trained on the same idea of realism, their distinct looks start to blur together. Bethesda responded to early Starfield footage by saying its art teams will tune the effect and that it will be optional for players, while Capcom reportedly wasn't aware(!) its game would appear in the demo at all.
Huang unfortunately made things much, much worse before he made them better, responding that "Well, first of all, they're completely wrong," when asked about the criticism during a GTC Q&A. His argument was that DLSS 5 operates at the geometry level under full developer control rather than as a filter slapped over finished frames.
Since the build leaked in late August, players have injected it into everything from Control to Monster Hunter Rise . Early testers criticized the Control mod's image quality and performance cost, but the same clips impressed enough gamers that TechRadar reported the first signs of the "negative tide turning." DLSS 5 is scheduled to be officially released this fall, with developer-tuned implementations that'll show whether NVIDIA's claims about developer control hold up better than its demos did.

title: Nvidia-Digital Realty AI Factory Buildout Runs Into Grid-Level Financing Test
text:
Nvidia-Digital Realty AI Factory Buildout Runs Into Grid-Level Financing Test
Nvidia and Digital Realty's push to build flexible AI computing infrastructure is facing obstacles that go beyond funding availability. A $150 million Series A for Emerald AI, announced in August at a $1.05 billion valuation, brought fresh capital but also revealed that a nearly 100-megawatt research facility in Manassas, Virginia, has slipped from its original first-half 2026 target to later this year. The core challenge involves operating AI infrastructure within power grid constraints while preserving computing performance. The grid squeeze is now measurable: three consecutive capacity auctions in the region covering the site have cleared at the maximum price regulators allow, and the last two fell short of the reliability standard. Emerald already reports commercial deployment at a California data center, validating the concept, but the Virginia project's economics remain unproven. Neither Nvidia nor Digital Realty has publicly commented. If constraints persist, they could slow new AI computing capacity, affecting cloud providers and enterprises that depend on expanded GPU access.
The push by Nvidia and Digital Realty to build flexible, large-scale AI computing infrastructure is encountering obstacles that go beyond the simple availability of cash, according to recent coverage. The challenge centers on whether their shared vision for an "AI factory" model can operate within the physical limits of the electrical grid while still delivering the computing performance customers expect.
A $150 million financing round for Emerald AI, announced August 25, brought fresh capital into the effort. The Series A valued the startup at $1.05 billion, was oversubscribed, and took total funding past $220 million. It was co-led by Energize Capital and DCVC, and Nvidia was joined by strategic backers including Samsung Ventures, Siemens, GE Vernova, RWE, Aramco Ventures and Salesforce Ventures; twelve Fortune Global 500 companies now hold investments in the company. The startup, whose orchestration technology coordinates computing workloads with onsite energy resources, said the funding would support commercial expansion. It also identified a nearly 100-megawatt research facility in Manassas, Virginia, being developed with Nvidia and Digital Realty, with an expected launch later this year.
The Virginia site is not a generic data center. Nvidia announced it in October 2025, at its GTC Washington event, as an AI factory research center at Digital Realty: the first deployment of infrastructure built around the Vera Rubin platform, the generation that follows Blackwell, and the proving ground for a design blueprint intended for gigawatt-scale build-outs. Emerald's facility, the Vera Rubin AI Research Factory, is being tested in collaboration with the Electric Power Research Institute, the utility Dominion Energy and PJM Interconnection, the grid operator whose capacity market the site must buy into.
The timing is significant. An earlier announcement in October 2025 had targeted the first half of 2026 for the Virginia project. The revised schedule suggests the buildout has slipped, though the companies have not publicly detailed the reasons. Reports from CryptoBriefing and Yahoo Finance frame the situation as a financing wall that additional capital alone cannot resolve, pointing to deeper structural friction rather than a straightforward funding shortfall.
AI data center projects demand enormous upfront investment in land, power infrastructure, and specialized hardware. Nvidia supplies the graphics processing units that power AI workloads, while Digital Realty operates the physical facilities that house them. Together, the two companies represent complementary halves of the AI compute supply chain. When financing hurdles extend beyond dollar amounts, they typically signal issues such as the pace of securing electrical power, permitting timelines, availability of suitable real estate, or the difficulty of matching long-term capital commitments to uncertain AI demand curves.
Those constraints have a price, and the price is now visible. PJM Interconnection operates the grid across 13 states and the District of Columbia, covering the Manassas site, and holds an annual auction to buy the generating capacity needed to keep the lights on. Three consecutive auctions have cleared at the maximum price federal regulators allow:
The 2027/2028 auction was the first in the market's history in which the entire footprint fell short of the standard, and the latest widened the gap; the operator has said it will seek approval for a special procurement this month to close the near-term hole. Data centers are driving the squeeze, accounting for nearly 5,100 of the roughly 5,250 megawatts by which the load forecast for the 2027/2028 delivery year was raised. "These auction results show that demand for electricity continues to grow faster than electricity supply," David Mills, the operator's president and chief executive, said in announcing the latest results. The International Energy Agency projects that data centers will account for nearly half of U.S. electricity demand growth between now and 2030.
The grid operator's response is where the Emerald thesis meets the market. PJM is developing "Connect and Manage" frameworks that would let large new loads such as data centers connect to the system but operate flexibly when the grid is stressed, and in June it began facilitating bilateral supply contracts for large customers that can run ten years or more. It has also opened an expedited interconnection track for shovel-ready generation projects sponsored by states. That points toward a regime in which a data center's speed of connection depends on its willingness to curtail — the capability Emerald sells.
Interconnection, meanwhile, is the slower constraint. Berkeley Lab counts about 2,061 gigawatts of generation and storage actively seeking a grid connection in the United States, down 10% from a year earlier and below the peak of nearly 2,600 gigawatts reached at the end of 2023. Only 13% of projects that filed interconnection requests between 2000 and 2020 had come online by the end of 2025, while 75% had withdrawn. The median project now takes well over three years just to sign an interconnection agreement and more than five years to reach commercial operation, and more than 40% of projects still fall away after an agreement is signed. That is the structural friction the coverage describes: a queue that capital alone cannot jump.
The proposed architecture is designed to let a facility adjust its electricity draw when the grid is under strain. Nvidia's software and infrastructure controls form part of the system, alongside Emerald's orchestration technology. For the chipmaker, successful deployments could ease a constraint on customers installing and using its systems, supporting demand through practical infrastructure availability rather than simply another investment in an AI startup.
Emerald already reports commercial deployment at an entire California data center, which validates the concept even if it does not establish the Virginia project's eventual economics. It says it has completed five demonstrations at commercial sites in Arizona, Illinois, Virginia, Oregon and London, working with the chipmaker as well as Oracle, Nebius and National Grid, and has partnered with Silicon Valley Power on what it describes as the first flexible-load interconnection program in the country, granting data centers expanded grid access in exchange for verified, dispatchable flexibility. A system that reduces electricity draw while disrupting valuable workloads would offer a weaker proposition. Wider adoption requires a workable balance between grid response and computing performance.
Digital Realty has a different route to value. Helping customers access power and operate reliably could strengthen the appeal of its facilities. Faster or more effective use of infrastructure can matter to a data-center REIT whose capital must eventually earn rental returns. However, the project announcement provides no quantified earnings contribution for Digital Realty, nor does Emerald's financing establish a new order value for Nvidia. The companies participate in the same technical effort without receiving identical financial benefits.
Investor positioning reflects ongoing interest in both names. Insider Monkey's database showed 285 hedge funds holding Nvidia in the second quarter of 2026, up from 275 in the first quarter. Digital Realty holders rose to 73 from 46 over the same period. Ken Fisher's firm held Nvidia, while Andreas Halvorsen's Viking Global held Digital Realty. Those positions predate the August financing. Short interest as of August 14 stood at 1.23% of Nvidia's float and 2.07% of Digital Realty's.
The strategic backers show where demand for that capability is expected to come from. Among them is the venture arm of JERA, Japan's largest power generation company, which describes itself as producing about one-third of the country's electricity; the fund has a stated strategic investment capacity of $300 million. Announcing the investment, JERA said grid interconnection constraints are emerging as a key challenge for data center development, and that software optimizing the interaction between computing workloads and the power system can play an important role in addressing them.
The AI infrastructure sector has drawn massive capital in recent years. Hyperscalers and specialized data center operators have committed billions of dollars toward expanding computing capacity. Nvidia's chips remain central to that expansion, given their dominant position in AI accelerator hardware. A financing wall at this stage would be notable precisely because so much capital has already flowed into the sector. It suggests that even well-capitalized, high-profile players face limits when scaling AI infrastructure at the pace the market has come to expect.
Neither Nvidia nor Digital Realty has publicly commented on the financing challenge, according to the available reports. Nor do the reports identify which lenders or investors, beyond Emerald's announced round, are involved.
For now, the story represents an early signal of friction in AI infrastructure financing rather than a definitive account of a stalled project. If constraints persist, they could slow the pace at which new AI computing capacity comes online. That would matter for cloud providers and enterprises depending on expanded GPU access to run AI workloads. Nvidia's hardware sales and Digital Realty's data center leasing business could both feel effects if large projects face delays.
The broader AI infrastructure sector, which has attracted significant investor interest, may also see closer scrutiny of how capital-intensive buildouts get funded. Investors watching AI-linked equities and infrastructure spending could treat this as a signal to examine execution risk more carefully, separate from headline capital commitments.
Further reporting will likely clarify what kind of structural or operational issue lies beneath the financing headline. The reports highlight friction in one of the AI industry's most closely watched infrastructure partnerships, and more detail is likely to emerge as the situation develops.

title: Musk highly confident SpaceX will launch Nvidia AI computers into orbit in 2027

Musk highly confident SpaceX will launch Nvidia AI computers into orbit in 2027
Elon Musk said he is highly confident SpaceX will launch Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 AI computers into orbit next year, part of its Starmind program targeting significant scale by 2028 and up to a million orbital data centres longer term.
Musk's comment reinforces a theme that has already moved both stocks once this year, when Nvidia rose more than 4% after SpaceX confirmed it would build exclusively on Nvidia hardware for its AI ambitions, while SpaceX shares initially fell over 10% before paring losses on investor uncertainty about execution risk and capital intensity. A reaffirmed 2027 launch timeline for the Starmind AI satellite keeps the Nvidia read through intact and gives some support to the idea that space based compute demand could become a durable, if still early stage, source of orders for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. For SpaceX specifically, the market's reaction is likely to hinge less on today's confidence signal and more on whether Starship's launch cadence and reliability can plausibly support the scale Musk is describing, given analyst modelling already extends capacity projections out to 2031 and the plan remains contingent on unresolved engineering questions around cooling, radiation hardening, and heat dissipation in orbit.

title: Nvidia Gets the AI Hype. Dell Gets the Billionaire Fortune

Nvidia makes the chips that run artificial intelligence (AI). Dell bolts those chips into metal racks and ships them.

title: Nvidia (NVDA) Looks Cheap on Piper’s Forecasts, but the Earnings Assumptions Are the Real Test
text:
After spending years trading like a premium-priced AI leader, Nvidia may now be among the cheapest names in Piper Sandler's AI universe. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ) is trading at an attractive valuation according to Piper Sandler's forecast, with rapid AI growth backing its trajectory.
On September 9, Piper Sandler analyst David O'Connor initiated coverage on NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) with an Overweight rating and a price target of $300, implying roughly 34% upside.
The firm believes that the chipmaker is an outright AI compute leader controlling 80% of the market by value and an estimated 50% by units. Owing to its annual cadence of next-generation products, it has been able to continue to drive the industry forward.
Piper Sees Nvidia Trading at Just 14x FY28 Earnings
Everyone knows and agrees that Nvidia has grown at an exponential pace. Its recent results offer evidence of operational strength as well. The company reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year-over-year.
The chipmaker's data center revenue also surged 117% to $89 billion. GAAP gross margin was75%, while adjusted diluted earnings reached $2.22 per share. The figures highlight how Nvidia's robust demand is translating into profitability for the company.
According to Piper's note, Nvidia trades near 14 times estimated fiscal 2028 earnings. The firm calls it among the cheapest valuations in its AI universe, implying a PEG ratio of 0.3. Its price target is based on the 14x multiple applied to its calendar 2028 estimates, suggesting the bullish thesis relies more on Nvidia delivering the expected growth rather than on substantial multiple expansion.
Supply Constraints Support Demand, but Execution Risk Remains
Piper Sandler believes that AI compute supply is likely to be constrained for the next two to three years. While scarcity supports demand visibility, it can also lead suppliers to plan capacity before all future sales are certain. The key test is for Nvidia to execute on its annual product cadence as competitors attempt to reduce dependence on its GPUs.
As per the company's latest filings, Nvidia reported $985 million of quarterly provisions for inventory and excess purchase obligations, partly offset by releases. There was also a disclosure of a first-half charge of about $400 million related to H200 products amid China sales restrictions. The figures reflect how demand doesn't always eliminate inventory and regulatory risks.
The Real Test Is Piper's 47% Growth Forecast
Piper Sandler estimates revenues growing at a 47% CAGR and earnings at a similar pace to $30 in FY30E.
Today's valuation looks inexpensive at that pace, but a meaningful slowdown in spending, product execution, or even profitability could make the 14x multiple less compelling.
In simple words, Piper's valuation depends heavily on its growth assumptions.
Hedge funds remain bullish on Nvidia's story. At the end of the second quarter, 285 hedge funds held Nvidia, up from 275 in Q1.
Overall, the firm's note is less a call about AI demand being strong and more about whether the company can continue compounding earnings at an exceptional rate while its valuation appears modest relative to Piper's growth assumptions.

title: Shiba Inu vs. Nvidia: Which Is More Likely to Win Over the Next 5 Years?
text:
Shiba Inu ( SHIB -0.30% ) was at one point the most high-octane cryptocurrency on the market. Its price absolutely skyrocketed in 2021, hitting a peak of $0.00008845 in October that year. It's been a slow downward trend since that all-time high was established. As of Sept. 11, Shiba Inu trades 94% off its record.
Nvidia ( NVDA +2.55% ) has been on a completely different trajectory. There has been insatiable demand for its data center chips during the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. This has made the stock an incredible winner, rising 860% during the past five years.
On one side, there's Shiba Inu looking to gain back its former glory. On the other side, Nvidia is riding the AI wave. Which investment opportunity is more likely to win during the next five years?
The meme token's best days are in the past
Shiba Inu's price has been disappointing. I believe this is representative of its investment case.
What propelled this meme token to fame was its strong community of supporters, known as the ShibArmy. The fact that the crypto's price has tanked means that this group's interest is waning. And it's silly for investors to bet their hard-earned savings on a reversal of fortune.
This is especially true when there aren't any convincing fundamentals to lean on. To its credit, Shiba Inu has a metaverse, Layer-2 scaling solution to handle more volume, and a decentralized exchange. None of these have done anything to lift the digital asset's price. Therefore, it's a valid assumption that adoption hasn't grown in any meaningful way.
There is simply way too much competition in meme-coin land these days. It's becoming obvious that Shiba Inu's best days are behind it. Long-term investors should avoid owning this crypto.
Demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure isn't slowing
At a $5.3 trillion market capitalization, Nvidia is the world's most valuable company. Its ascent has been remarkable to watch. AI has been the single most important driving force.
Nvidia sits right in the middle of the AI boom. It sells the most powerful and highly sought after graphics processing units (GPUs) that support AI training and inference. And its CUDA software enables developers to create various applications.
Demand for data center GPUs has been phenomenal. The biggest customers are the hyperscalers , as well as neocloud, industrial, and enterprise clients. All want access to computing capacity, which is in extremely short supply these days.
It's difficult to comprehend just how impressive Nvidia's growth has been. Revenue more than doubled year over year in the latest fiscal quarter (Q2 2027 ended July 26). Net income surged 126%.
The shares trade at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 24.6. This represents a 16% premium relative to the S&P 500 index. That's a compelling valuation given how robust Nvidia's financial performance has been.
Clearly, the market isn't fully appreciating the business. Any rational investor could come up with a valid argument as to why the forward P/E multiple should be double where it currently stands. Just look at the company's revenue and earnings growth.
However, this highlights the biggest risk factor. No one knows the durability of the AI infrastructure build-out. We're in uncharted territory here. There's a chance that the music stops before anyone anticipates, at which point Nvidia's financials would be adversely affected. It's important not to ignore this possibility.
Only one of these opportunities deserves a serious look
During the next five years (or any timeframe for that matter), Nvidia has much greater upside than Shiba Inu. In fact, there's a strong likelihood that the meme coin will be worth less in the future, as interest continues to fade.
Nvidia's valuation is cheap relative to its monster financial success. But the stock's performance is entirely dependent on the AI boom lasting for a long time. Any notable slowdown can pressure the shares. Prospective investors should understand the thesis before buying the business.

title: Nvidia and Australian partners target 2GW AI buildout
text:
Nvidia and eight Australian cloud and data-center companies are working toward an AI-infrastructure buildout of up to 2 gigawatts by 2027. The companies plan to use Nvidia’s DSX platform in facilities run by the local providers, according to a September 9 company announcement .
The partners named are Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC and AirTrunk. Nvidia said it would supply computing, networking, software and ecosystem support, while the operators would run the AI factories. The 2GW figure is a target for the combined buildout, not capacity already in service. Reuters reported the expansion on September 10.
Firmus is expanding Project Southgate, its Australian AI-factory program. The company has also announced a separate deal to supply OpenAI with computing capacity from two planned sites in Malaysia. Nvidia’s new announcement concerns the Australian ecosystem; it does not say that the Malaysian sites are included in the 2GW target.
Sharon AI said it is deploying up to 68,000 Nvidia GPUs with Quantum InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet networking. The announcement does not specify how many of those processors have been installed, the timetable for the full deployment or Sharon AI’s share of the proposed 2GW. IREN described its 800-megawatt Bundey campus in South Australia as part of its development portfolio using Nvidia’s AI-factory architecture. That campus figure is a project capacity, not an additional confirmed amount to add to the coalition-wide target.
CDC said its facilities across Australia and New Zealand currently operate more than 550 megawatts of capacity, with a further 800 megawatts under construction. Its existing and in-construction figures describe CDC’s broader portfolio; Nvidia did not say all of that capacity would be dedicated to DSX AI factories. NEXTDC cited its liquid-cooled facilities and cloud interconnections, while AirTrunk described plans to expand AI-ready powered shells with direct-to-chip liquid cooling.
Megaport said its Latitude.sh subsidiary would extend access to accelerated computing for inference workloads through the company’s network. ResetData described an AI-cloud offering for customers requiring Australian data residency. These roles range from providing land and powered facilities to delivering computing and connectivity, rather than a single construction project under Nvidia’s ownership.
Nvidia describes DSX as a full-stack platform spanning facility designs, computing, networking and software. The company says broader domestic access to AI compute could serve startups, universities, researchers and enterprises. It also named Australian companies Heidi and Atlassian as users of its Nemotron models and other AI tools. Their model-development work is distinct from commitments to buy capacity at the proposed facilities.
The announcement does not provide a site-by-site power allocation, aggregate investment amount, financing breakdown or construction schedule for each operator. It also does not identify the share of the 2GW that already has grid connections, planning approvals, contracted customers or installed Nvidia systems. The proposed timetable therefore depends on work by several independent operators and the availability of power and supporting infrastructure.
Reuters noted that Australia’s current data-center capacity is about 1.6GW, citing industry group Data Centres Australia. That countrywide estimate is a separate measure from Nvidia’s proposed AI-focused buildout and should not be read as a direct before-and-after count of operational compute. Nvidia said its facilities could support both Australian users and wider Asia-Pacific demand.
Firmus already has a substantial regional footprint, including its planned Indonesian expansion, but Nvidia’s September announcement is centered on Australian capacity. The companies have not disclosed whether any Southeast Asian project would count toward the 2GW Australian target.
